Police Oversight Task Force 
January 8, 2014 
5:30 p.m. 
 
Summary Minutes 
 
 
 
 
Members present*: 
Frances Armijo  
Ralph Arellanes  
Fabrizio Bertoletti 
Hans Erickson  
Nancy Koenigsberg 
Andrew Lipman  
Craig Loy 
Edmund Perea 
Peter Simonson  
Alan Wagman  
Leonard Waites 
Council staff present: 
Stephanie Yara 
Jessica Gonzales 
Donna Montoya
 
 
Others present: 
Dr. Bruce Perlman, School of Public Administration, UNM 
Timothy Karpoff 
  
*Reflects members present when the meeting is called to order. Any excused absences 
will be reflected in actions taken in the summary minutes. 
 
 
 
1. 
Call to order 
 
Mr. Lipman called the meeting to order at 5:37 p.m. 
 
2. 
Approval of Agenda 
 
Mr. Loy made a motion to approve the agenda. It was seconded by Ms. Armijo.  
The motion passed unanimously. (Mr. Erickson and Mr. Wagman were 
excused). 
 
 
 
3.  
Approval of Summary Minutes 
 
 
 
 
Mr. Loy made a motion to approve the December 18, 2013 summary minutes.  
 
 
 
It was seconded by Mr. Waites. The motion passed 9-1 (Mr. Bertoletti abstained).

4. 
Public Comment 
 
 
Don Schrader addressed the Police Oversight Task Force (POTF) regarding the use 
of non-deadly weapons, allow more time for police negotiations, childhood post-
traumatic stress disorder, and the need for the public to recognize the use of non-
violence by police officers. 
 
 
Tad Niemyjski addressed the POTF regarding City Council Bill R-14-10 “Endorsing 
The Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Center’s Task Force For Public Safety 
Recommendations Regarding The Selection Of The New Chief Of Police For The City 
Of Albuquerque”. 
 
 
Charles Arasim encouraged the POTF to attend the Police Oversight Commission 
(POC) meeting to listen to the discussion on the emails he submitted, and the appeal 
that was deferred for the lack of information to the applicant. 
 
 
Stephanie Lopez addressed the POTF regarding Mr. Lipman’s statements to the 
media with regards to APD’s problems. Ms. Lopez added the POTF should be 
unbiased and balanced. 
 
 
Mr. Lipman reported that he attended the City Council meeting on January 6, 2014, 
and asked Councilor Sanchez to follow-up on a letter from the POTF to the Mayor.  
 
Mr. Lipman also reported that he was invited to attend the Department of Justice 
(DOJ) meeting which was very well covered by the media, but no findings were 
presented. 
 
 
Mr. Simonson stated that the DOJ final recommendations will benefit the Police, and 
that Mr. Lipman does not have to explain his role as a member of the POTF. 
 
 
Mr. Lipman stated that he is un-biased, a facilitator, and that he did not say anything 
inflammatory.  
 
 
 
5. 
Discussion – Final Town Hall meeting 
 
 
Mr. Lipman announced that the discussion on the final Town Hall meeting will be 
postponed to a later date. 
 
 
 
6. 
Recommendation Facilitation – Timothy Karpoff 
 
 
Mr. Karpoff ran a facilitated discussion on the key questions that the POTF’s 
recommendations must address. (see attachment A)

 Mr. Lipman announced the following POTF meetings: 
• January 15, 2014, 5:30 p.m., Council Committee Room 
• January 21, 2014, 5:30 p.m., Council Committee Room 
• January 29, 2014, 5:30 p.m., CIP (7th floor) Conference Room

None

4. 
Public Comment 
 
 
Richard Shine addressed the Task Force regarding the IRO and the POC having 
subpoena powers, access to investigative files, and for the POC to have the authority 
to take testimony, and administer oaths. 
 
Tad Niemyjski addressed the Task Force regarding a Police incident that he 
witnessed on Second Street.  
 
 
 
5. 
Recommendation Facilitation – Timothy Karpoff 
 
a. Draft Recommendations from the January 15, 2014 Meeting 
 
 
Mr. Karpoff ran a facilitated discussion on the draft recommendations and made 
amendments which Ms. Yara will incorporate and provide to the members. 
(Attachment A). 
 
b. Preamble 
 
A motion was made by Ms. Koenigsberg to accept the Statement of Principles 
(formally known as the Preamble). The motion was seconded by Mr. Wagman.  
The motion passed unanimously.  Mr. Simonson was excused. (Attachment B). 
 
Ms. Koenigsberg asked for recommendations from the City Council once the final 
report from the POTF is reviewed. Mr. Lipman responded that request will be included 
in the cover letter to the City Council. 
 
 
 
6. 
Announcement of Upcoming Meetings 
 
 
 
 
 Mr. Lipman announced the following POTF meeting: 
 
 January 29, 2014, 5:30 p.m., Council Committee Room (9th Floor) 
 
 
 
 
 
Mr. Lipman asked Dr. Perlman to email the “final” draft report to the POTF for their  
 
 
review prior to their next meeting. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 9:22 p.m.

4. 
Public Comment 
 
 
Jonathan Siegal addressed the Council regarding the size of a new oversight agency. 
He feels nine members would be more beneficial than seven, with three being 
selected by the Mayor, three selected by the City Council, and three selected by 
outside interested citizen groups. 
 
 
Charles Arasim and Tad Niemyjski addressed the Council regarding qualifications for 
Oversight Commission members and that they live within the jurisdiction of APD 
officers. 
  
 
 
Richard Shine addressed the Task Force regarding a possible new compromise on 
dealing with the Garrity issue more effectively. He provided a handout of his 
comments. 
 
 
Nora Anaya addressed the Council regarding information made available to citizens 
from APD. She would also like to see drug testing of all APD officers. 
 
 
 
5. 
Recommendation Facilitation – Timothy Karpoff 
 
 
Mr. Karpoff ran a facilitated discussion on the draft recommendations and made 
amendments which Ms. Yara will incorporate and provide to the members. 
 
 
A motion was made by Ms. Koenigsberg to vote on final recommendations at the next 
meeting on January 21, 2013. The motion passed unanimously.  Mr. Simonson and 
Mr. Arellanes were excused. 
 
 
 
6. 
Announcement of Upcoming Meetings 
 
 
 
 
 Mr. Lipman announced the following POTF meetings: 
 
• January 21, 2014, 5:30 p.m., Council Committee Room 
• January 29, 2014, 5:30 p.m., CIP (7th floor) Conference Room 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 9:15 p.m.

POLICE OVERSIGHT TASKFORCE 
AGENDA 
Wednesday August 6, 2014  
5:30 p.m. – 7:30 p.m. 
Council Committee Room, City Hall, 9th Floor Room 9081 
 
 
1. Call Meeting to Order – Andrew Lipman – 5:30 p.m. 
2. Approval of Agenda – 5:30 – 5:35 p.m. 
3. Approval of Summary Minutes July 23, 2014 – 5:35 – 5:40 p.m.  
4. Final Review of Police Oversight Ordinance amendment recommendations – 5:40 
a. Number of POB Members.  
b. Selection and removal of POB Members. 
c. Subject matter experts on POB. 
d. POB involvement with initial investigations and Public Letter Records. 
e. POB access to full investigative files. 
f. RO discussion of findings with APD Chief before finalization.
